stem: What is Static Site Generation (SSG)?
options: Pre-rendering all pages as static HTML at build time — served directly from a CDN without server computation

stem: What is "First Contentful Paint" (FCP)?
options: The time until the browser renders the first piece of content (text, image) from the server response

stem: What is the main SEO benefit of SSR?
options: SSR apps have smaller JavaScript bundles
Search engine crawlers can read fully-rendered HTML without executing JavaScript
SSR apps load faster on mobile

stem: What is "Time to Interactive" (TTI)?
options: Time until the first pixel is rendered
Time until the page is fully interactive — JavaScript loaded, hydrated, event handlers attached

stem: What is the "hydration mismatch" problem?
options: When CSS doesn't match the JavaScript
When server-rendered HTML doesn't match what the client-side framework tries to hydrate — causing re-rendering
When the hydration script is too large
When localStorage doesn't match server state

stem: What is Next.js?
options: A React framework supporting SSR, SSG, and hybrid rendering with file-based routing

stem: What is Nuxt.js?
options: A Vue.js framework with SSR, SSG, and hybrid rendering capabilities

stem: What does `getServerSideProps` do in Next.js?
options: Fetches data on the server for each request, injecting it as props into the page component for SSR

stem: What does `getStaticProps` do in Next.js?
options: Fetches data at build time — the page is statically generated with the data and served as pre-built HTML

stem: What is "Incremental Static Regeneration" (ISR)?
options: Regenerating all pages on each request
Statically generating pages that are periodically regenerated in the background — combining SSG performance with fresh data

stem: What is "streaming SSR"?
options: Sending HTML in chunks as they're rendered on the server — the browser can paint content before the full response completes

stem: What is `<Suspense>` in React's SSR context?
options: A boundary that defers rendering of slow-loading components — in SSR, streams a placeholder until the component's data is ready

stem: What are "meta tags" and why are they important for SSR?
options: Tags in `<head>` (title, description, og:image) that must be rendered server-side for SEO and social media sharing

stem: What is "data fetching strategy" for SSR?
options: How data is cached in localStorage
Deciding whether data is fetched on the server (SSR), at build time (SSG), on the client (CSR), or using ISR

stem: What is the "flash of unstyled content" (FOUC) problem in SSR?
options: After SSR HTML loads, if CSS loads late or hydration causes style changes, there's a visual flash

stem: What is "edge rendering" / "edge SSR"?
options: Running SSR at geographically distributed edge servers (like Cloudflare Workers) close to users — reducing latency

stem: What is "progressive enhancement" in SSR context?
options: Starting with working server-rendered HTML, then enhancing with JavaScript — the app works even if JavaScript fails

stem: What is `renderToString` in React?
options: Converts a React component to a CSS string
Renders a React component tree to an HTML string on the server — for SSR
Converts React to plain HTML files

stem: What is the "Time to First Byte" (TTFB)?
options: Time until the first CSS rule applies
Time from the request until the browser receives the first byte of the server response
Time for the first JavaScript to execute
Time for the first API response

stem: What is the "uncanny valley" of hydration?
options: The period between FCP (users see content) and TTI (page is interactive) — the page looks ready but clicks don't work

stem: What is "partial SSR" (hybrid rendering)?
options: Rendering half the CSS on the server
Rendering some routes with SSR, some with SSG, some with CSR — per-route rendering strategy optimization

stem: What is "server components" (React Server Components)?
options: Components that run only in Node.js
Components that render on the server only — never hydrated, never sending JavaScript to the client

stem: What is the main performance challenge of SSR?
options: Every request requires server computation — high traffic can strain the server; SSG or caching mitigates this
JavaScript bundles are larger with SSR

stem: What does `useEffect` do differently on the server during SSR?
options: `useEffect` doesn't run on the server — effects only execute in the browser environment after hydration
Throws an error on the server

stem: What is "SvelteKit"?
options: The official Svelte meta-framework supporting SSR, SSG, file-based routing, and full-stack development

stem: What does `dehydrate` / `rehydrate` mean in React Query SSR?
options: Serializing server-side cached query results to JSON for HTML embedding, then restoring them on the client
Refreshing all queries on the client

stem: What is "Astro" and its approach to SSR?
options: A web framework using "islands architecture" — SSG by default, with opt-in hydration for interactive components

stem: What is a "bundler" in the context of JavaScript development?
options: A tool that packages npm modules
A tool that combines JavaScript modules and assets into optimized bundles for production

stem: What is Vite?
options: A fast modern build tool using native ES modules in development and Rollup for production builds

stem: What is Webpack?
options: A mature, configurable bundler that creates a dependency graph of all project assets and bundles them

stem: What is Rollup?
options: A JavaScript bundler optimized for library bundling — producing clean, tree-shakeable ES module output

stem: What is "transpilation"?
options: Converting modern JavaScript (ES2022+, TypeScript, JSX) to older JavaScript compatible with more browsers
Converting TypeScript types to runtime checks

stem: What is "tree shaking"?
options: Eliminating unused code (dead code) from the final bundle by analyzing static imports

stem: What is "code splitting"?
options: Dividing the bundle into smaller chunks that are loaded on demand rather than all upfront
Dividing a component into smaller components

stem: What is "minification"?
options: Removing whitespace, comments, and shortening variable names in JavaScript/CSS to reduce file size

stem: What is a "source map"?
options: A map of all source files
A file mapping minified/transpiled code back to the original source — enabling debuggable production code

stem: What are "environment variables" in build context?
options: Values injected at build time (API URLs, feature flags) that differ between development and production

stem: What does Babel do?
options: Transpiles modern JavaScript and JSX to backwards-compatible JavaScript

stem: What is "Hot Module Replacement" (HMR)?
options: A dev server feature that replaces only changed modules in the browser without a full page reload

stem: What is the difference between `devDependencies` and `dependencies` in package.json?
options: `dependencies` are needed at runtime; `devDependencies` are only needed during development/build (Babel, Webpack, TypeScript)

stem: What is "lazy loading" in the build context?
options: Splitting code into chunks and loading them only when needed — reducing initial JavaScript parse/execute time

stem: What is the purpose of `.browserslistrc` or `targets` configuration?
options: Telling Babel/PostCSS which browsers to support — determining how much transpilation is needed

stem: What is "chunk hashing" in production builds?
options: Adding a hash of the file content to the filename (e.g., `main.a3f4b2.js`) for cache busting

stem: What is `esbuild`?
options: An extremely fast JavaScript bundler and minifier written in Go — used internally by Vite and other tools

stem: What is "dead code elimination"?
options: Automatically removing code that can never be executed — unreachable branches, unused functions

stem: What is a "production build" vs "development build"?
options: Production is minified, tree-shaken, and optimized; development has source maps, HMR, and verbose error messages

stem: What is "CDN" (Content Delivery Network) for static assets?
options: A geographically distributed network of servers hosting static assets close to users — reducing latency

stem: What is "gzip" or "Brotli" compression?
options: Server-side compression of text files (JS, CSS, HTML) before sending to browsers — reducing transfer size

stem: What is "Prettier" in a build pipeline?
options: An opinionated code formatter — enforces consistent code style automatically

stem: What is "ESLint" in a build pipeline?
options: A configurable JavaScript/TypeScript linter — catches bugs, enforces code quality rules

stem: What is `vite.config.js` used for?
options: Configuring Vite's build behavior, plugins, resolve aliases, dev server settings, and build output

stem: What is "SWC"?
options: A super-fast Rust-based JavaScript/TypeScript compiler — a faster alternative to Babel

stem: What is "bundle analysis"?
options: Visualizing what's in a production bundle — identifying large dependencies and optimization opportunities

stem: What is "TypeScript" in the build pipeline context?
options: A typed superset of JavaScript compiled to plain JavaScript at build time — providing static type checking

stem: What is "PostCSS"?
options: A tool for transforming CSS with JavaScript plugins — autoprefixer, CSS nesting, custom properties polyfills

stem: What does the `public` directory in Vite/Next.js do?
options: Contains static assets (images, fonts, favicon) served directly at the root URL, not processed by the bundler

stem: What are "deployment strategies" for a built SPA?
options: Methods for serving the production build — static hosting (Netlify, Vercel), CDN, server (Node.js), container (Docker)
Vite with React plugin, `@` alias for `/src`, output to `dist`, with source maps in production
